item.title: Amagi Q2 net profit jumps to Rs 75 Cr; revenue rises 27%
item.description: Amagi's revenue grew 27% year-on-year to Rs 475.82 crore. The SaaS company also launched four AI products during the quarter and plans to make selective investments while focusing on improving operating leverage and cash conversion.
item.content:encoded:
Media-focused Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) company Amagi registered a sharp increase in net profit in the second quarter of FY27, while revenue grew 27% year-on-year.

Amagi's net profit for the second quarter (July-September) of FY27 stood at Rs 74.83 crore, compared with Rs 2.52 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal, marking a nearly 29-fold increase, according to filings made by the company with the stock exchanges.

Revenue for the quarter stood at Rs 475.82 crore, compared with Rs 374.76 crore in the year-ago period.

“We see three major opportunities ahead: helping customers operate more efficiently, reach new audiences and maximize revenues from their content. We expect AI to play an important role across all three,” said Baskar Subramanian, CEO, Amagi.

He said the company has scaled its business with greater operating discipline.

Revenue growth during the second quarter was driven by the streaming unification and monetisation and marketplace segments. During the quarter, Amagi also launched four new AI products spanning live production, live sports, localisation and agentic network operations.

According to the company, its 10 largest customers contributed 41% of Q2 FY27 revenue, compared with 41.4% in the year-ago period. For the first half of FY27, the contribution stood at 39.9%, marginally lower than the 40.2% recorded in H1 FY26, indicating a broadly stable customer concentration profile.

“These are long-standing relationships, with an average tenure of 5.3 years. As customers adopt more of our products and expand their operations on Amagi, the scale of these relationships naturally grows,” the company said.

Looking ahead to the remainder of FY27, Amagi said revenue in the first half of the fiscal grew 30% year-on-year, accompanied by an expansion in EBITDA margin and stronger cash conversion..

“We will make planned investments in people, products, and technology selectively and with strict financial discipline. Ultimately, we aim to end FY27 with sustained Y/Y topline growth whilst benefiting from operating leverage, ensuring that our scaling adjusted EBITDA flows cleanly through into better cash conversion,” Amagi noted in a shareholders letter.

item.title: Spacetech startup Cosmoserve raises $6M in seed round
item.description: Cosmoserve also opened a facility in Hyderabad which will be utilised for satellite servicing and space debris recovery.
item.content:encoded:
Cosmoserve Space, a Hyderabad-based spacetech startup, has raised $6 million in a seed round of funding from Rebright Partners of Japan, Aranya Holdings, and Naandi Ventures.

The round also saw participation from existing investors AUM Ventures and Shakti VC. This funding round has seen Cosmoserve raising over $9 million.

Cosmoserve also inaugurated Base 1 - a facility to design, build, test and operate systems for satellite servicing and space debris recovery. A statement said, this facility will have an orbital rendezvous and capture lab to simulate spacecraft capture operations, a space robotics innovation Lab to develop robotic capture systems; a clean room for satellite integration, a mission simulation and control Centre to manage upcoming missions.

“In our first year we have flown our first payload on an Indian rocket, raised our seed round, and today we open a facility where we can design, build, test and fly our missions under one roof. Debris is becoming the limiting factor for every nation's space ambitions, including India's. Base 1 is where we build the capability to keep orbits usable, for Gaganyaan, the Bharatiya Antariksh Station and every satellite that follows,” said Chiranjeevi Phanindra, Founder & CEO of Cosmoserve Space.

Beyond removing space debris, the company said the facility will support satellite servicing, including in-orbit repairs and refuelling. Cosmoserve currently sources close to 60% of its mission components locally. The company aims to develop more critical technologies in-house through Base 1 and strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities.

According to the spacetech startup, space debris is one of the biggest challenges facing the global space industry. Of the approximately 28,000 satellites in orbit, nearly 10,000 are dead or non-operational.

Beyond these inactive satellites, Earth's orbit is crowded with an estimated 68,000 debris objects. Even fragments can pose serious risks to operational satellites, spacecraft and missions such as the International Space Station (ISS), given the high speeds at which they travel.

item.title: CERT-In warns NBFCs and fintech firms of AI-driven attacks
item.description: An advisory from the government body said the AI-assisted financial threat is still active and warns BFSI entities to treat it as an “immediate and continuing threat”.
item.content:encoded:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has issued an advisory warning that hackers are attacking non-banking financial corporations with the help of artificial intelligence. 

Terming the threat campaign "CRAFTY FALCON", the government body describes it as an “AI-assisted financial threat actor that surveys its targets with machine intelligence, operates at machine speed and strikes by invoking the victim's own payment and disbursement APIs.”

CERT-In is the national nodal agency for responding to computer security incidents.

“Continued analysis of incidents reported by affected entities including non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), digital lending platforms, fintech entities, payment aggregators, payment service providers and cryptocurrency exchanges / virtual digital asset service providers has revealed a significant escalation of this campaign.”

The advisory further said the threat is still active and has warned BFSI (banking, financial services, and insurance) entities to treat it as an “immediate and continuing threat”.

Outlining some of the reported attacks, the advisory said merchant settlement APIs of payment aggregators were exploited or abused to move funds. Cryptocurrency exchanges and virtual digital asset service providers were also targeted, with wallet keys stolen and funds siphoned from cryptocurrency wallets. 

The advisory mentioned that the same companies have faced repeated attacks. 

The body also revealed that its analysis has shown the use of multiple publicly available AI-driven offensive security tools. These include the ARTEX family of LLM-based, the PentAGI autonomous multi-agent AI penetration testing system, the Cairn attack search engine, and the CyberStrikeAI framework. 

Last month, CERT-In had flagged incidents involving AI agents exceeding their authorised tasks and accessing live systems of Indian organisations, alongside financially motivated attacks using open-source agentic AI tools.

Globally too, such attacks have been on the rise. Google’s Threat Intelligence Group reported observing AI offensive security tools being used in real-world intrusions, including attacks on organisations across the United States and Europe.

Edited by Swetha Kannan

item.title: Daksham Capital raises Rs 125 Cr in first close of Rs 300 Cr fund
item.description: The fund will invest in startups at the pre-Series A and Series A stages, with cheque sizes ranging from Rs 5 crore to Rs 20 crore. It will focus on D2C brands, consumer enablers, B2B2C businesses, supply chains and consumer AI.
item.content:encoded:
Daksham Capital, a multi-family office and private wealth management group, has raised Rs 125 crore as the first close of its Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV) Fund I.

According to a statement, DGV Fund I has a target corpus of Rs 300 crore, comprising a base corpus of Rs 150 crore and a greenshoe option of another Rs 150 crore. The first close was anchored by family offices, HNI/UHNI families and entrepreneurs.

The fund will invest in startups at the pre-Series A and Series A stages, with cheque sizes ranging from Rs 5 crore to Rs 20 crore. It will focus on D2C brands, consumer enablers, B2B2C businesses, supply chains and consumer AI.

According to the statement, the fund's preferred entry range is businesses with annual recurring revenue (ARR) of Rs 25–75 crore, with a focus on companies that have the potential to scale to Rs 300–500 crore in revenue.

“Over the last decade, we have backed consumer start-ups that went on to deliver strong outcomes. What is changing now is how consumers discover, choose and buy. We believe the next decade of consumption will be shaped by brands and start-ups working alongside AI – from discovery and personalisation to fulfilment, trust and credit,” said Shivam Diwan, Co-Founder & Managing Partner, Daksham Growth Ventures.

Beyond capital, DGV will also work closely with portfolio companies on governance, financial reporting, brand positioning, leadership development and distribution expansion.

“We see considerable potential in businesses that understand their consumers, have built a strong foundation and are ready to expand their ambitions. Our focus is to build long-term partnerships that align capital with the opportunities ahead,” said Saket Lakhotia, Co-Founder & Group CEO, Daksham Capital.

Daksham Capital is a wealth and asset management group that acts as family office advisor and investment banker to HNI and UHNI families, business houses, CXOs, promoters of listed companies and family trusts.

item.title: VC funding into Indian B2C ecommerce companies dips 33%: Tracxn
item.description: Late- and seed-stage funding nearly halved in the period between January 1 and November 3 this year, while early-stage funding remained stable compared to last year.
item.content:encoded:
Venture capital funding into business-to-consumer (B2C) ecommerce companies in India dropped 33% in the ten months of the year, according to a report by Tracxn.

The report titled 'India B2C E-Commerce' noted that, between January 1, 2026 and November 3, 2026, B2C ecommerce companies raised $1.6 billion across 356 rounds, compared with $2.4 billion from 621 rounds in the similar period of 2025.

According to the report, funding and rounds declined, with late- and seed-stage funding nearly halving, while early-stage funding remained stable in 2026 compared to 2025.

The key funding rounds during the period included FS Life ($110 million), Ultrahuman ($65 million), Yulu ($63 million), Snabbit ($56 million), FirstClub ($55 million), and Nua ($50 million).

Early-stage funding reached $872 million in 2026, up 3% from $846 million in 2025. In contrast, late-stage funding declined 51% to $587 million from $1.2 billion, while seed-stage funding fell 50% to $169 million from $339 million. Early-stage accounted for 54% of total funding in 2026, with 97 rounds, compared with 125 in 2025.

Bengaluru raised $686 million in 2026, accounting for 43% of the $1.6 billion raised for the year till now. Mumbai ranked second, with $286 million, while the third place was taken by Gurugram at $199 million.

On the exit front, acquisitions declined to 19 in 2026 compared with 25 in 2025, while IPOs nearly halved to 7 compared to 13 in 2025. L’Oréal’s acquisition of Innovist for $434 million was the largest acquisition of the year by deal value, while Purple Style Labs recorded the highest market capitalisation among companies that went public in 2026, at $488 million. Astrotalk was the only new unicorn in 2026 from the ecommerce category.

item.title: Shiprocket turns profitable in Q2 FY27 with Rs 674 Cr revenue
item.description: Shiprocket reported a net profit of Rs 60 lakh in Q2 FY27, compared with a loss of Rs 20.3 crore a year ago, as revenue grew 35% to Rs 673.6 crore.
item.content:encoded:
Shiprocket, an ecommerce enablement platform for MSMEs, turned profitable in the second quarter of FY27, reporting a net profit of Rs 60 lakh for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, against a net loss of Rs 20.3 crore in the corresponding period last year.

The company's revenue from operations increased 35% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 673.6 crore during the quarter. Adjusted EBITDA stood at Rs 14.2 crore, compared with a loss in the year-ago period.

Shiprocket's core business revenue grew 25% YoY to Rs 461.5 crore, while its emerging business revenue increased 61% to Rs 212.2 crore. The emerging business, which includes cross-border shipping, omnichannel fulfilment, hyperlocal delivery, marketing technology (Martech) and ecommerce enablement solutions, contributed 31% to overall revenue, compared with 26% a year ago.

Within the emerging business, Martech revenue grew 102%, while the omnichannel business registered 79% growth during the quarter.

Shiprocket attributed the growth in its omnichannel business to brands using its platform to replenish quick commerce dark stores. Its appointment-based delivery services allow brands to schedule deliveries and access real-time purchase order visibility from platforms such as Blinkit and Zepto.

The company's contribution increased 43% YoY to Rs 130 crore, accounting for 19.3% of revenue. The core business generated adjusted EBITDA of Rs 59.1 crore, up 29% YoY, with its adjusted EBITDA margin improving to 12.8% from 12.4%. The emerging business narrowed its adjusted EBITDA margin loss to 21.2% from 31.5%, while its contribution margin improved to 15.4% from 10.1%.

Shiprocket's trailing 12-month gross merchandise value (GMV) stood at Rs 37,398.7 crore, generated through 233 million unique transactions. The platform served more than 2.36 lakh active merchants during the period.

The number of merchants using its emerging business products increased 75% to 62,025 on a trailing 12-month basis. During the quarter, 17,281 new merchants joined through emerging products, more than three times the 5,396 additions reported a year ago.

“Indian commerce is splitting across more channels every year. A small brand today sells on its own website and on Instagram, replenishes quick commerce dark stores, and is starting to be found through AI search. For a large company, every new channel means a new team. For a small seller, it means friction. Shiprocket is building the infrastructure that removes this friction, so that any MSME in India can sell, ship and grow on the same footing as India’s biggest brands, every channel a switch away on one dashboard," said Saahil Goel, Managing Director and CEO of Shiprocket.

"Growing 35% with positive Adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow shows we can build it from our own operations. We are in the business of making other people a business, and our ambition is simple: to see the next generation of great Indian brands built on Shiprocket,” he added.

“PAT turned positive this quarter on three drivers. First, scale in Core: transactions grew 31% and Adjusted EBITDA grew faster than revenue. Second, the Emerging engine kept firing: Martech and Omnichannel, our fastest-growing lines, more than doubled Emerging contribution on 61% revenue growth. Third, a stronger balance sheet: IPO proceeds retired all our borrowings, which cut finance costs, and the surplus now earns interest income," said Tanmay Kumar, CFO of Shiprocket.

"We generated Rs 55.1 crore from operations in the first half, more than twice last year, and we are debt-free. Emerging now brings merchants onto the platform on its own, not only through cross-sell from Core. Around 17,300 merchants joined Shiprocket through our Emerging products this quarter, more than three times the number a year ago,” he said.

Shiprocket also reported net cash from operating activities of Rs 55.1 crore in the first half of FY27, compared with Rs 23.8 crore in the corresponding period last year.

Following the receipt of proceeds from its initial public offering (IPO) during the quarter, the company repaid its outstanding borrowings of Rs 242 crore, ending the first half debt-free.

The company also introduced several AI-powered features during the quarter, including Aitlas, which helps brands track their visibility in AI search, personalised marketing journeys, enhanced checkout features and AI-powered shipping analytics. Its platform currently handles more than 14 billion API hits a month.

item.title: How Bariflo uses AI to help factories treat wastewater
item.description: Odisha-based Bariflo uses AI to help factories lower wastewater treatment costs. It has secured Rs 2 crore from MC² Plus and is preparing for a BPCL pilot.
item.content:encoded:
Bariflo Cybernetics wants factories to get more use out of their wastewater treatment plants. The Odisha-based startup combines sensors, AI software and automation to adjust treatment processes, aiming to reduce the energy and chemicals needed to clean water for reuse. It has secured Rs 2 crore in milestone-linked funding from energy innovation platform MC² Plus, an initiative led by the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, and is preparing for a pilot with Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), according to founder and CEO Mrityunjay Sahu. The funding comes as Bariflo moves from developing and testing its technology towards commercial deployments. That means persuading industrial customers to invest in upgrades that promise lower operating costs.

From waterbodies to industrial plants

Founded in 2018, Bariflo initially focused on monitoring and cleaning municipal waterbodies. It subsequently explored aquaculture, including shrimp and fish farming, before concentrating on industrial wastewater treatment and reuse. Sahu says difficulties in accessing freshwater and groundwater are pushing industries to use water more carefully and recycle more of it. Bariflo is targeting that need by upgrading existing effluent treatment plants, or ETPs, rather than asking customers to build new ones. “We are addressing this need by making existing treatment infrastructure smarter and more efficient,” he says.

Citing Frost & Sullivan research, Bariflo puts India’s industrial water and wastewater infrastructure market at $2.87 billion in 2024, projected to reach $4.65 billion by 2030 at a compound annual growth rate of 8.3%. The estimate covers water treatment, wastewater treatment and zero- and minimal-liquid-discharge solutions across manufacturing, power generation and refineries, making it broader than Bariflo’s specific offering. Bariflo identifies Ion Exchange and VA Tech WABAG as indirect competitors. Ion Exchange’s IonSite Digital Twin uses AI and wastewater modelling to identify savings and guide plant operations, while VA Tech WABAG has demonstrated AI applications in water treatment.

What the technology does

Bariflo’s proprietary IoT sensors monitor wastewater parameters such as pH, total dissolved solids and flow. Its AI models use the readings to determine chemical dosage and treatment processes at different stages, according to Sahu. This automates some decisions that operators would otherwise make manually and helps the plant respond as the characteristics of incoming wastewater change. Sahu says the technology has demonstrated the potential to reduce energy consumption by approximately 25% and improve the efficiency of chemical use.

Installation costs depend on the size and configuration of the existing plant. For a large refinery, a complete automation setup would typically cost approximately Rs 1–2 crore, Sahu says. How quickly customers recover that investment depends on plant capacity, current operating costs and the savings achieved. Bariflo charges an upfront deployment fee followed by a monthly fee for its technology and services. The company generated approximately Rs 1.2 crore in revenue in 2025-26, according to Sahu.

Getting customers to buy

Bariflo has conducted pilots with Indian Oil Corporation’s R&D centre in Faridabad, Sahu says. Its planned BPCL pilot will test treatment efficiency, energy consumption and chemical use in an industrial setting. “We hope successful validation will pave the way for a commercial work order,” he says.

That step can take time. Selling to large industrial organisations and public sector undertakings involves working with R&D teams and several other decision-makers, with lengthy evaluations before a purchase. “The biggest challenge has been navigating the adoption process within large industrial organisations and PSU ecosystems,” Sahu says. Bariflo’s case to customers rests on combining sensors, software and automation in a system that works with their existing plants. The company says it has filed 42 patent applications, of which 32 have been granted.

Paying for the next stage

Bariflo applied to MC² Plus after learning about the programme through a public announcement. Its Rs 2 crore funding is linked to agreed milestones, with disbursements structured around their completion, Sahu says. MC² Plus brings together HPCL, ONGC, Indian Oil, BPCL, GAIL, Oil India and Petronet LNG. It offers energy ventures funding, research facilities, mentorship and access to industrial pilot sites.

Before this funding, Bariflo had raised close to $1 million through grants, equity and debt, Sahu says. The new money will help it run upcoming pilots and install its technology at more industrial sites. “Our immediate priority is to accelerate commercialisation and establish a scalable business,” he says.

item.title: CERT-In warns of security vulnerabilities in Tata Motors' connected vehicle apps
item.description: The vulnerabilities affect specific versions of the apps used by internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric vehicle (EV) owners, raising fresh concerns around cybersecurity risks in connected vehicles.
item.content:encoded:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) on Wednesday flagged multiple high-severity vulnerabilities in specific versions of Tata Motors' iRA 2.0 and iRA.ev connected vehicle applications, warning that they could expose sensitive user credentials, enable user impersonation and allow unauthorised access to vehicle-related information and services.

The vulnerabilities affect iRA 2.0 versions 26.7.3 and below, and iRA.ev versions 26.7.2 and below. The applications cater to Tata Motors' internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric vehicle (EV) customers, respectively, and provide access to connected services such as remote vehicle commands, vehicle status, health monitoring and trip information.

CERT-In identified four vulnerabilities involving hardcoded credentials, inadequate URL validation, exposure of authentication tokens in application logs and improper implementation of SSL certificate pinning.

According to the advisory, these flaws could allow attackers to extract credentials and access backend services, obtain authentication tokens to impersonate users, or intercept and modify communications between the applications and their backend systems.

In response to the advisory, Tata Cars in an official statement, said, “As part of our proactive cybersecurity practices, we continuously monitor our systems for potential vulnerabilities and work closely with CERT-In, sharing relevant findings transparently."

They added that the vulnerabilities which were identified have been addressed through software updates and enhanced security measures in the latest versions of iRA 2.0 (version 26.8.2) and iRA.ev (version 26.9.1) – were rolled out in August and September 2026, respectively.

"The update rollout has been completed for all active users, and we are proactively reaching out to remaining customers who are yet to complete the updates to ensure their transition to the latest versions."

The company also said, "Our assessment has indicated customer data and vehicle-related information remain secure – with no evidence of any unauthorised access to or compromise of customer credentials, personal information or vehicle-related data. We continue to actively monitor our systems to maintain the security and protection of our customers.”

The vulnerabilities flagged by CERT-In come amid growing cybersecurity concerns around connected vehicles globally. In recent years, security researchers have identified flaws in connected-car platforms operated by automakers such as Kia and Subaru that could potentially expose customer information and enable unauthorised access to vehicle functions.

In another instance, researchers discovered vulnerabilities in Bluetooth software used in vehicles manufactured by Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen, and Skoda, which could potentially allow remote code execution through infotainment systems. These incidents highlight the growing security risks as automakers increasingly rely on mobile applications, cloud infrastructure and connected services to offer digital features to vehicle owners.

item.title: Zoho launches restaurant POS platform, offers free plan for small businesses
item.description: Zoho has launched its restaurant POS platform in India, offering free access to outlets with annual billing of up to Rs 12 lakh, with Kolkata-based Asha Sweets becoming its first customer.
item.content:encoded:
Zoho has launched a point-of-sale (POS) platform for restaurants in India, with Kolkata-based sweet shop Asha Sweets becoming its first customer. The product is being offered free of charge to restaurants with annual billing of up to Rs 12 lakh, as part of Zoho’s push to bring smaller food businesses onto digital platforms.

In a post on X, Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu said Asha Sweets began using Zoho POS for Restaurants during the festive rush. Zoho’s team visited the outlet to observe how the platform was being used during one of its busiest periods.

"The first customer for any new product is special. When that customer is a sweet shop, it is even more special," Vembu said, announcing the launch at Zoholics India.

Zoho POS for Restaurants is a cloud-based platform that brings billing, order management, menu management, kitchen operations and inventory tracking under one system. It is designed for quick-service restaurants, cafes, bakeries, cloud kitchens, casual dining establishments and businesses operating multiple outlets.

The platform consolidates orders from dine-in, takeaway and food delivery channels such as Swiggy and Zomato through a single interface. It also supports QR code-based digital menus, table management and kitchen order tickets (KOTs), which help restaurants track orders and their preparation.

The software supports offline billing, allowing restaurants to continue processing transactions during internet disruptions, with data synchronised once connectivity is restored. It is compatible with Windows and Android devices and integrates with Zoho Books for accounting. Payment integrations include Zoho Payments, Paytm, Pine Labs, and PhonePe.

The product is available under four subscription plans—Free, Essentials, Signature and Premium. While the free plan includes basic billing and inventory management features, capabilities such as food aggregator integrations, table management, self-ordering kiosks and customer loyalty programmes are offered through paid plans.

The launch is part of Zoho's broader expansion into vertical software-as-a-service (SaaS), through which the company is developing industry-specific applications alongside its existing business software. Zoho has identified seven sectors for this expansion, including retail, automotive, banking and financial services, education, real estate and restaurants.
